evidence: Liv. 1.13.4: silentium et repentīna fit quiēs
terms.comment: Of people and of places. silentiō or per silentium, “in silence”; silentium facere, “to call for silence” (see quiet!); silentium tenēre (Livy), “to keep silent”; silentia rumpere, “to break the silence”, is poetic.
A person’s silence, not speaking or not telling; silentium is the stillness itself.

evidence: Phaedr. 1.2.17: tacitē prōfert ē stagnō caput
terms.comment: Also secretly, unnoticed. The adjective tacitus goes with the person: Tacitus citius audiēs (Ter. Eun. 571).

phrases.english: there is silence, and a sudden calm
the crested cocks have not yet broken the silence

phrases.latin: arripuī, aperuī, et lēgī in silentiō
phrases.english: I snatched it up, opened it and read in silence
